converter: cth_convert_sym_v8.py (a copy of docx_text() of the workbench converter harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py that also maps Symbol-font and private-use characters; kept outside the repository); the first deposit used harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py

symbol_repair_2026_11_07.previous_converter: harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py (docx_text), the converter of the 2026-10-13 deposit
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.from: the same Word files of C2026C00260 (C2026C00260VOL01.docx and C2026C00260VOL02.docx, joined sha256 a69049a11a7ba7f57d7854b2997b861381d41f3ade421b8d5ba33dbae03cce35, this deposit's download_sha256)
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: docx_text() dropped characters Word writes as Symbol-font w:sym elements. cth_convert_sym_v8.py maps them to Unicode (Symbol F0D6 √, F0B4 × and the like), Wingdings boxes to "[ ]", and private-use code points U+F0xx the same way; run with its mapping switched off it reproduces the first deposit byte for byte.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: Five tick marks (Symbol F0D6 -> √, used as the tick in the printed forms) restored in Schedule 1 (Forms), in the candidates' statements of the nomination forms: lines 9509 and 9535 (Nomination of a Senator), 9554 (Nomination of Senators), 9590 and 9615 (Nomination of a Member of the House of Representatives): "Please tick []" -> "Please tick [√]". A diff against the first deposit shows no other change (same 14,245 lines, five characters more). Line numbers are unchanged.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.encodings_affected: none: no rule, case or finding of baseline-2026-10 or naive-2026-10 relies on the Schedule 1 forms (both encode Form DB's checklist only as a fact asked, from s 170)
